paths.description: Homepage and sole discovered endpoint. It represents the entire observed site because the DOM has no internal links, the manifest is absent, robots.txt and sitemap.xml return only generic “empty OK” text, and arbitrary routes receive the same catch-all response. Not covered: authenticated or undiscoverable routes, because none were linked or declared.

findings.summary: Dark preference still produces a white canvas
findings.evidence: The dark-preference screenshot remains a blank white canvas; the rendered body has a transparent background and black text with no color-scheme declaration.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare `color-scheme: light dark` and provide preference-driven surface/text colors using `light-dark()` or `prefers-color-scheme`.

findings.summary: No state or route interaction exists to feel natural
findings.evidence: There are no links, controls, state changes, routes, or authored CSS/JS, so the default natural-interaction outcome is absent rather than implemented.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore a meaningful primary interaction and use progressive, reduced-motion-aware View Transitions where its state or route changes would otherwise be abrupt.

findings.summary: The page provides no navigation or orientation cues
findings.evidence: The page has no navigation, in-page links, headings, or focusable destinations, so it cannot guide attention or orientation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add descriptive navigation and a clear primary destination, with visible focus and state cues that show where attention moved.

findings.summary: Mobile browsers fall back to a 980 px layout viewport
findings.evidence: The page has no viewport meta tag; Chrome therefore lays it out at 980 CSS px and scales it to 360 px. There is no overflow only because the response is empty.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">` and use intrinsic fluid layout once content is restored.

findings.summary: The public homepage is completely blank
findings.evidence: The 200 response renders a completely blank page with no title, heading, text, navigation, or action.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish meaningful server-rendered HTML with a descriptive h1, concise purpose statement, and an obvious primary action.

findings.summary: No user journey can start or complete
findings.evidence: No primary task can begin: the page has no content, links, forms, controls, or routes.
findings.suggestedFix: Define the site’s primary task and provide a complete, crawlable path through real links/forms with predictable completion.

findings.summary: No empty, error, or recovery state is presented
findings.evidence: A fabricated missing path returns HTTP 200 and the text “empty OK”; the homepage provides no loading, empty, error, success, retry, or recovery state.
findings.suggestedFix: Return intentional states with clear status text and recovery links/actions; distinguish empty content from errors.

findings.summary: The page never paints content, so FCP and LCP do not exist
findings.evidence: The trace recorded no FCP or LCP, and Lighthouse terminated with NO_FCP because the page never painted content. A blank response cannot satisfy the content-paint performance outcome.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore meaningful HTML content and prioritize its critical text/media so the page produces an early FCP and LCP, then re-run field/lab metrics.

findings.summary: The document has no h1 or main landmark
findings.evidence: axe reports missing main landmark and missing h1; the DOM has zero headings and landmarks.
findings.suggestedFix: Structure restored content with one clear h1 and a `<main>` landmark, then verify heading order and keyboard focus.

findings.summary: Missing viewport metadata breaks true mobile reflow
findings.evidence: There is no viewport meta tag, causing a 980 CSS px layout viewport under 360x800 mobile emulation. There are no targets or media requiring separate checks.
findings.suggestedFix: Add the standard responsive viewport meta tag without disabling user scaling, then verify reflow and target sizing at narrow/zoomed conditions.

findings.summary: The server sends a zero-byte document without doctype or charset
findings.evidence: The zero-byte response has no doctype or declared charset; Chrome falls back to windows-1252. There are no images or authored assets.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a valid HTML document beginning with `<!doctype html>` and `<meta charset="utf-8">`; send a single correct `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` header.

findings.summary: Title and meta description are absent
findings.evidence: The document title is empty and no meta description exists in either the rendered DOM or zero-byte raw response.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a unique descriptive `<title>` and meta description that accurately summarize the restored visible page.

findings.summary: No links or valid robots policy exist, and viewport metadata is absent
findings.evidence: There are no crawlable links or descriptive link text and no viewport meta tag. /robots.txt returns a generic 200 “empty OK” body rather than a robots policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Use descriptive `<a href>` links, add viewport metadata, and serve a valid plain-text robots.txt policy.

findings.summary: Canonical, sitemap, and HTTP indexing signals are malformed or absent
findings.evidence: The page has no canonical or hreflang; robots.txt and sitemap.xml both return generic “empty OK” text, and a fabricated missing URL returns 200 rather than 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Return correct status codes, publish a valid robots.txt and XML sitemap, and add a canonical URL where duplication is possible.

findings.summary: Core transport and content security headers are missing
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used and no cookies or mixed-content requests exist, but CSP, HSTS, and X-Content-Type-Options are all missing.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep HTTPS and add HSTS, a restrictive Content-Security-Policy, and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; set any future cookies Secure and SameSite.

findings.summary: Clickjacking, referrer, and permissions defenses are absent
findings.evidence: HSTS, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy are absent; no CSP frame-ancestors policy exists.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP `frame-ancestors` (or X-Frame-Options fallback), a strict Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: No core content exists with or without JavaScript
findings.evidence: The successful raw response is zero bytes and the rendered DOM is equally empty, so no core content or primary flow survives with or without JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Start with meaningful server-rendered HTML and layer JavaScript enhancements on top so core purpose and navigation survive script failure.

findings.summary: Unknown URLs return a misleading 200 “empty OK” response
findings.evidence: A fabricated missing path returns HTTP 200 with “empty OK” rather than a 404 page or useful recovery options.
findings.suggestedFix: Return HTTP 404 for unknown routes and render a useful not-found page with navigation back to a working destination.

findings.summary: The root document does not declare language or direction
findings.evidence: The html element has no lang or dir attribute; axe reports html-has-lang as serious. There is no authored CSS to inspect for logical properties.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an accurate `<html lang>` and, when needed, `dir`; use logical CSS properties when layout is added.

taskList.title: Replace the zero-byte catch-all with meaningful, valid, server-rendered HTML
Add responsive viewport metadata and verify mobile reflow
Return correct error statuses and a useful recovery page
Deploy baseline security and defensive browser headers
Respect the user’s light/dark color preference
